Why do some population groups experience systematically worse health than others? This course examines the causes, measurement, and policy implications of health inequalities, with a particular focus on the role of public policy.

The course combines a **conceptual part** with an **applied empirical part**. Students work with cross-national survey data from the International Social Survey Programme (ISSP) and the European Social Survey (ESS) and develop their own empirical research project over the semester.
